aj: Quick share — I ran a targeted sweep on canary nodes to investigate recent tail latency blips. Summary: p95 up ~12% for requests with seq >1024 when kernel-selector falls back to the int8-fallback kernel during short high-load bursts. Suspect interaction between batchshape skew (many tiny requests mixed with a few long ones) and kv-cache miss bursts.
sara: Oof. Do you have the trace ids / span snippets?
aj: Yes — attaching minimal spans and a couple PromQL snippets. Example trace: span shows long wait in scheduler queue then kernel switch.
henrietta: Can you paste the PromQL you used for the histograms? want to try the dash locally.
aj: PromQL I used for queue wait histogram (we bucket by queue_wait_ms):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(queue_wait_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route, kernel_variant))
```
And batch-size distribution:
```
sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route)
```
Also a counter to correlate kernel choice: `kernel_choice_total{kernel="int8-fallback"}` vs `kernel_choice_total{kernel="fp16-opt"}`.
mike: Two quick asks: 1) can we add a label for kv_hit=(hit|miss) on the queue_wait metrics? 2) can the sampler emit batch_shape percentiles (e.g. p25/p50/p75) per route?
aj: Agree on labels. For kv_hit it's cheap to add at enqueue time. Batch_shape percentiles — sampler currently only emits histograms, but we can add aggregated gauges from the sampler process.
henrietta: For dashboards I propose three panels per route: 1) token-level latency breakdown (enqueue / queue_wait / kernel_exec / kv_lookup), 2) batch size histogram + p50/p90, 3) kernel-selector heatmap (kernel vs seq_len bucket vs kv_hit).
sara: For token-level breakdown, can we surface average kv latency (ms/token) separately? ops wants to see if kv miss storms align with tail tokens.
aj: Yeah — we already have kv_lookup_ms_bucket. PromQL to join kv misses and queue wait spike:
```
sum(rate(kv_lookup_ms_sum[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(kv_lookup_ms_count[5m])) by (route)
```
Then overlay with p95(queue_wait_ms).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout 17 -> 20: kernel-selector-change deployed to group B.
ops-signal-bot: Alert suppressed: transient queue_wait spike in canary group B (1999512368) — auto-snooze 10m.
mike: If we add kv_hit label on queue_wait, be careful about cardinality explosion — only add hit|miss and keep route/model tags minimal. Also ensure we don't tag by request_id.
aj: Good call. We'll emit queue_wait_ms_bucket{kv_hit="hit|miss", route, model, kernel_variant}. No per-request tags.
henrietta: For the kernel-selector heatmap, we should bucket seq_len by [<=64, <=256, <=1024, <=2048, >2048], and compute kernel_choice fraction per bucket.
aj: Proposed SQL-ish aggregation for dash backend: `count_over_time(kernel_choice_total{kernel="int8-fallback"}[10m]) / count_over_time(kernel_choice_total[10m]) by (seq_bucket)` — will translate to PromQL.
sara: Timeline? can we have a first-pass dash tomorrow for eng oncall?
aj: I can push a draft to grafana tonight if no objections. Will also add a small profiler marker in sampler to emit batch_shape_gauge.p50/p90 per route.
mike: Sounds good. If kernel switch is correlated with kv-miss bursts we should consider temporary fallback policy: if kv_miss_rate > 10% and queue_wait_p95 > 50ms, prefer fp16-opt kernel for long-seq to avoid extra decode overhead.
aj: Noted. I'll add an experiment flag to the selector and run A/B on canary.
henrietta: Thanks — once draft dash ready, ping #eng-sre and I'll take a look. :thumbsup:
sara: Thanks!
